records.issue_text: remove_member renders success even when user_id was never a member; group.save is a no-op returning true, giving no feedback distinguishing removed from wasn't-there
records.rationale:
In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code unconditionally does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds (which it typically will even if nothing changed):

```rb
group.users.delete(user_id)
if group.save
  render json: success_json
end
```

So the endpoint does not distinguish “user was removed” vs “user_id was not a member” (no check on delete result / membership), which is a concrete API/UX semantics concern. The diff does not establish that this is incorrect behavior (it may be intended to be idempotent), so it’s not a provable defect

records.issue_text: removeMember/addMembers reload doesn't re-clamp offset against new page count, so removing a member while on the last page can land on a blank page
records.rationale: `removeMember`/`addMembers` call `self.findMembers()` after changing membership (group.js: `removeMember`/`addMembers`), but `findMembers()` only clamps `offset` against the *current* `user_count` before the request (`offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`). After a removal, `user_count` is stale until the response arrives, so it can request an `offset` that is now past the end of the list. records.issue_text: Unbounded, unvalidated limit/offset parameters in groups_controller.rb members action allow any authenticated user to request the entire membership list in one query, enabling DoS and bulk user-enumeration on large automatic groups
records.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then executes `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound or validation on `limit` (and no sanity check on `offset`). This allows a client to pass an arbitrarily large `limit` to fetch huge membership pages in a single query/response, which can enable DoS and bulk enumeration for any group the requester can see (`guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`).
